::: {.exam-question}
## Question {.question-label}

[**Outline**]{.task-verb} the factors that determine recovery (offset of action) after ceasing a drug infusion.
:::

Also asked in: [2002A Question 10](/content/exams/anzca/2002/A/10/index.qmd#examiner-comments)

## Examiner Comments

::: {.examiner-comments}
The pass rate for this question was **55%**. As always, it was disappointing to see that several candidates had failed to plan the examination, and had left little or no time to answer the final question.

An ideal answer would have considered the offset of infusion effects in terms of both pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. Kinetic parameters of importance include re-distribution and clearance. Pharmacodynamic effects would have led to a consideration of the interactions with other drugs. Good answers used several examples, the commonest used being propofol, remifentanil and non-depolarizing muscle relaxants. Answers (and there were many) which concentrated purely on the issue of context-sensitive half time and remifentanil attested more to successful marketing by drug companies, rather than a clear understanding by candidates of the issues raised by this question.
:::
